newsitem.title: USA: SBC files to offer Oklahoma long distance.
newsitem.headline: SBC files to offer Oklahoma long distance.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc said on Friday its Southwestern Bell unit filed a Federal Communications Commission application to offer long-distance telephone service in Oklahoma.

SBC already offers long distance in Oklahoma to cellular customers but is seeking to expand its service. The filing for long distance is the first by SBC in its traditional five-state territory, which also includes Texas, Missouri, Kansas and Arkansas.
SBC said that in coming months it planned to file to offer long-distance service in the other states.
The company said the FCC has 90 days to rule on the Oklahoma filing.
SBC also said it has signed interconnection and resale agreements with 16 companies seeking to provide local telephone service in Oklahoma.

"The Telecommunications Act of 1996 requires Southwestern Bell to open the local market to new competitors in order to enter the long-distance business," said Dale "Zeke" Robertson, an SBC senior vice president, in a statement.
SBC shares closed Friday at 50-7/8, down 1-1/8 for the day.
